defects.evidence: `read_k120` computes `passes` for all six kernels, bandwidth.c lines 418 to 444 return `2 * cfg.bytes` per pass for copy and asmcopy, and line 32 of threads120.csv of T72A1 (copy) gives 128849018880 / 268435456 = 480.

defects.before: Coordinated Universal Time. All times in the run files are UTC.
defects.after: Coordinated Universal Time. All dates and times of day in the run files are UTC. The values `t_start_s` and `t_end_s` of a T row are not times of day. They count the seconds from the process start.
defects.evidence: Line 2 of a6456.csv says "times are seconds since process start" and bwx12.c lines 3083 to 3084 print `t_start - t_base_ns`, so the universal statement did not hold for the T-row times that this companion explains.

defects.after: New word "Data set": a named group of interval records. `build_facts.py` writes the name into the key `dataset` of each record [Ref3]. The files of the rerun give four data sets: `rerun-A`, `rerun-L`, `rerun-C` and `control-I`. Each one holds the intervals of all result folders of that part. The earlier runs have other names, for example `A-1` and `L-1`.
defects.evidence: The heading of lines 386 to 392 and two call_sequence notes use "data set" without a definition, and build_facts.py lines 166, 177, 201, 253 and 280 set the names (facts.json holds 216, 30, 24 and 20 records for the four names of the rerun).

defects.before: - A P row holds the page state of one buffer. It is stored as a tuple: round, pos, thread, buffer letter and the 6 numbers of fields 6 to 11 (the first two are `kB_total` and `kB_huge`).
defects.after: The same text, followed by: The buffer letter is `a` for the first buffer of a thread and `b` for its second buffer. The 9 bwx12 csv files of the rerun hold only `a` rows.
defects.evidence: "Buffer letter" had no meaning in the text; bwx12.c line 3117 prints `i % 2 ? 'b' : 'a'` for the buffers `th[i].a` and `th[i].b`, and field 5 is `a` in all 9960 P rows of the 9 csv files of the rerun.
